newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's AWB sells 4,000/t wheat in tender 33.
newsitem.headline: Australia's AWB sells 4,000/t wheat in tender 33.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Tuesday it had sold 4,000 tonnes of wheat in its latest tender for domestic sales from the national pool.
Total bids were received for 194,000 tonnes.
In this, bids were for 10,000 tonnes of current season wheat and 184,000 tonnes of new crop wheat.

Lowest successful bids were priced at A$210.00 a tonne for Australian Standard White (ASW) current crop delivered Port Kembla and A$220.00 a tonne for current crop Australian Hard wheat delivered Newcastle.
The focus of tender participants was swinging further to new crop supply, AWB said in a statement on the results.

Australia's east coast required substantial rain to shore up current crop forecasts, it said. It was evident from recent tenders that concerns on the availability of particular grades in certain zones were rising.

Note: ASW = Australian Standard White; AH1 = Australian Hard 1. Next tender: August 21
